analysis: The only change is documentation in docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new table row at head line 119, 'Provider-staged destinations'. The row describes the provider-staged, non-native-bound complete-checkpoint import. It says staging builds destinations from zeroed host bytes and skips eval and stream fences, so it never waits on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. It also says the import plan charges the largest destination as staging scratch. No code is in this PR, so no security behavior changes here. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the row's remaining code references are not visible. Relevant threat IDs: T-041 and TB-007, whose cache surface, staging reservations and no-persistent-carve posture are unchanged. DBK3 authentication, HMAC lookup tags, TTL and identity binding are unchanged. Open question for deeper review: the corresponding Swift change, in CheckpointHostZeros.swift and the import plan, is not supplied. Cross-pass reviewers should check that the claimed scratch charge for the transient zero-source commit is actually enforced in the host memory budget (GlobalKVCacheBudget), and that skipping eval/fences cannot expose uninitialized or stale GPU memory. This is a code-side concern; the doc alone is not evidence of a regression. The document drift risk is low, and no threat-model update is needed from this doc-only change.
